subject: Day 40: daylight stroller loop
bodyText:
Today's focus
Week 6 is the first sustainable inflection point: crying is at or just past peak, and a daily daylight stroller loop now does triple duty for Avi's sensory input, Anoushka's cardiovascular recovery, and the household's routine.

Action items
- Walk a 20-30 minute daylight stroller loop most days. It delivers varied sensory input for Avi, supports Anoushka's gradual return to activity, and resets the afternoon for everyone. AAP HealthyChildren: Vitamin D: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/healthy-living/nutrition/Pages/Vitamin-D-On-the-Double.aspx
- Keep giving Avi 400 IU/day of vitamin D if he is exclusively or predominantly breastfed. Sun exposure on a stroller walk does not replace the supplement, since infants should stay out of direct sun. AAP HealthyChildren: Vitamin D: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/healthy-living/nutrition/Pages/Vitamin-D-On-the-Double.aspx
- Confirm Avi's 2-month well visit is booked. The window is day 56-70, and the first rotavirus dose must be given by roughly day 104, so do not let it slip much past day 70. AAP periodicity schedule: https://www.aap.org/en/practice-management/care-delivery-approaches/periodicity-schedule/

Watch-fors
- [low concern] Hiccups during or after feeds, wet sneezing, and a quiet startle on loud sounds are all normal this week.
- [monitor] No social smile yet. Many infants smile by now, but flag it at the 2-month visit if it has not appeared by 8 weeks.
- [call within 24h] A cluster of new symptoms together, such as poor feeding plus lethargy plus a clear drop in wet diapers.
- [call now] Rectal temperature of 100.4F (38.0C) or higher in an infant under 3 months, blue color around the lips, or labored breathing. For blue lips or an unresponsive episode, call 911 now!

Enrichment opportunities
- Sing a slow walking tune live during the stroller loop, varying the genre day to day. Live serve-and-return singing, not recorded audio, is the active ingredient for early auditory and language development. PubMed: infant music perception: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/22490184/
- Bring one board book and read a couple of pages on a bench stop. Daily shared reading builds the pre-literacy foundation pediatricians now treat as a routine prescription. AAP early literacy: https://www.aap.org/en/patient-care/early-childhood/early-literacy/
- Position the stroller so Avi faces varied scenery and shade rather than the same canopy, giving his sharpening visual tracking new contrast and motion to follow. AAP HealthyChildren: baby senses: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/ages-stages/baby/Pages/default.aspx

Upcoming
- Day 41 (Jun 21): Anoushka's 6-week postpartum visit, with expected exercise clearance, contraception discussion, and a final EPDS mood screen.
- Day 56-70 (Jul 6-20): 2-month well visit; vaccines due are HepB #2, RV #1, DTaP #1, Hib #1, PCV #1, and IPV #1.
- Day 57-72 (Jul 7-22): the 24-48h window after the shots, when low-grade fever, drowsiness, and fussiness are expected.
- Day 112-126 (Aug 31-Sep 14): 4-month well visit with the second vaccine round.

Developmental milestone check-in
Tap any link to mark it complete. View or change others at https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones

- Looks at a toy for several seconds
  AAP window: day 35-60
  What to look for: Sustained visual attention — precedes reaching.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/2-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/looks-at-toy-several-seconds/complete

- Coos or makes sounds beyond crying
  AAP window: day 35-60
  What to look for: Vowel sounds like ooh, ahh. Pre-language vocalization. Distinct from fussing or hiccup sounds.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/2-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/coos-makes-sounds/complete

- Holds head up while on tummy
  AAP window: day 35-60
  What to look for: Sustained head lift of several seconds, not just a brief bob. Forearms may or may not be supporting yet.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/2-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/holds-head-up-tummy/complete

- Hands relax open most of the time
  AAP window: day 35-90
  What to look for: Newborn fists relax as the palmar grasp reflex fades. Predictor of voluntary grasp coming.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/2-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/hands-open-mostly/complete

- First social smile (responding to a face, not gas)
  AAP window: day 28-60
  What to look for: Smile in response to someone smiling or talking to them, not a reflexive gas smile. Hallmark social milestone.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/2-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/first-social-smile/complete
